advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm '(failure)' is intended to veto ALL rejection lines carrying that reason token, or scope it to the GitHub 'fatal error in commit_refs' co-occurrence so it cannot over-match.
evidence: src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_ref_lock.py:735: _NON_CAS_REJECT_MARKERS += ("fatal error in commit_refs", "(failure)")  # bug ebee: GH 5xx
src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_ref_lock.py:744: if _LEASE_MISMATCH_MARKER in stderr: return True (checked before the veto markers, so 'stale info' still wins)
'! [remote rejected] <sha> -> ref (failure)' — '(failure)' is git's generic reason token, not GitHub-specific
advisory.finding: The new '(failure)' entry in _NON_CAS_REJECT_MARKERS is a very broad substring: git renders every rejection reason as '(<reason>)', so any '! [remote rejected] ... (failure)' line now vetoes CAS-mismatch classification. It is safe today only because a genuine --force-with-lease rejection always prints '(stale info)', which _is_cas_mismatch_stderr short-circuits on first — but the marker's breadth is not self-documenting and could silently mask a future CAS-relevant rejection whose reason string happens to embed 'failure'.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a backoff test that drives >= 4 consecutive CAS recoveries to exercise the _cas_backoff index-clamp branch (attempt >= len(_CAS_BACKOFF_SECONDS)).
evidence: push.py:528 `for attempt in range(1, _MAX_RETRIES + 1):` with push_classify.py:145 `_MAX_RETRIES = 5` — attempt reaches 5, beyond the 4-element schedule
test drives only 2 recoveries: `results = [1, 1, 0]` and asserts `slept == list(push_classify._CAS_BACKOFF_SECONDS[:2])` (tests/unit/test_push_strict.py), never reaching attempt >= 4
advisory.finding: The clamping branch of _cas_backoff (attempt >= len(_CAS_BACKOFF_SECONDS)) is never exercised. _MAX_RETRIES=5 but _CAS_BACKOFF_SECONDS has 4 entries, so attempts 4 and 5 rely on the min(attempt, len(...))-1 clamp; the only backoff test drives just 2 recoveries (results=[1,1,0]), leaving the index-clamp path (and its IndexError risk) untested.
scenarios: A 4th or 5th consecutive lost CAS race in production hits the clamp branch that no test covers; an off-by-one there IndexErrors mid-recovery.
advisory.suggested_fix: Parametrize or extend test_lost_cas_race_backs_off_between_retries with a run that recovers 5 times (results all 1 until attempt 5) and assert slept equals _CAS_BACKOFF_SECONDS clamped to its last value for the tail attempts.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether the escalating CAS backoff should also apply on a False (retryable) recovery, not only a clean-merge True, since both paths re-push on the next loop iteration.
evidence: src/rebar/_store/push.py:374:  # ... back off before the caller re-pushes
src/rebar/_store/push_classify.py:352: ``True`` means a clean merge, ``False`` means a retryable local recovery failure
src/rebar/_store/push.py:562: if recovered is None: return  (False falls through to loop, next iteration re-pushes with no backoff)
dropped.finding: _cas_backoff is invoked only when _merge_remote_under_lock returns a truthy value; when recovery returns False (a retryable local recovery failure such as a merge-conflict path), the loop re-pushes on the next iteration with no backoff — contradicting the comment 'back off before the caller re-pushes' and leaving the exact back-to-back re-collision the change set out to fix for that class.
